target_questions.question: Does crossing from subsonic to supersonic post-shock flow materially change the early deformation/drag response?
target_questions.target_basis: Tier 1 C007 flags compressibility effects, while C025 provides shock-Mach breakup chronology; this study isolates early-stage response.

evidence_candidates.claim_text: For the simulated early breakup of water cylinders, transition to supersonic post-shock flow did not markedly change scaled drift, acceleration, or drag, and deformed diameter improved the near-constant drag representation.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: Numerical reproduction of shock-tube experiments extends the incident-Mach range and tests early-stage scaling across the sonic transition.

core_links.shared_parameter_or_mechanism: compressibility effects on droplet breakup response

limitations: Two-dimensional water-cylinder geometry and early breakup only; this does not adjudicate later supersonic compressibility effects.
visual_verification: Targeted visual verification performed where numeric/glyph-dependent abstract claims required it; no figure digitization.
